subject: 80/20 Rule Applied to Open Source Shiny Server Security

messages.author: de0353bdfec15530
messages.subject: 80/20 Rule Applied to Open Source Shiny Server Security
parts:
Hello all.  Let me describe my scenario / use case.

I have an Apache server running as a reverse proxy to the open source version of Shiny server.  My use case is for research, specifically to allow researchers to collaborate and openly share data.  There isn't any sensitive data in my app (e.g. financial information, personal health information), however, I still want to take the necessary precautions in securing the Shiny server to prevent it from being hijacked.  There are obviously guides for securing an Apache server, which I am going through before making my app public, but even if my Apache server is secure, my understanding is that my Shiny server could still potentially be exploited if there are vulnerabilities.  In particular, I am interested in expending 20% of the effort to make my server 80% safe, since I am quite busy, as I imagine many others on this forum are as well. 

Has anyone went through this process and is also willing to give some tips on securing an Apache + Shiny server combo?

Do any guides exist for securing a Shiny server?

What are the most important quick and dirty tips for securing an Apache + Shiny Server combo?

At some point I might want to implement users/passwords/authentication, which I see there have been some posts on this topic already on this forum.  What has worked for people using this model?

Thanks!  I hope this can help serve the community as a quick guide to (mostly) securing a private Shiny Server.
